transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic? What's been concerning you?

I... well, I guess I'm here because of work. Things have been difficult lately. Ever since I got that county safety award, certain people have been... twisting my inspection reports. Asking all these pointed budget questions. 

It's like they're trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor keeps telling me it's just a normal review, but... I know what I see. It's pretty obvious there's a coordinated effort to discredit me. 

I don't really want to get into all the details right now, but... that's what's going on.
When you say people are twisting your reports and trying to discredit you, do you have specific examples or documentation of this happening, or is it more of a sense you have about what's going on?

I... I don't have the paperwork with me. But it's not just a feeling. 

It's... it's the way they ask the questions. About the budget. About the inspections. It started right after I got that county safety award. It's just... it's obvious to me. Even if my supervisor says it's a normal review, I know what a normal review looks like. This isn't it. 

They're trying to make me look crooked. I just... I know they are. I'd rather not get into the specifics of the reports right now.

If your supervisor or someone you trust completely told you that this coordinated effort to discredit you wasn't actually happening, could you consider that possibility, or are you completely certain it's real?

I... my supervisor already told me that. He said it's just a normal review. But... I can't just ignore what's right in front of me. 

I know what I see. Ever since I got that county award, the way they twist my inspection reports... asking those pointed budget questions... it's obvious they're trying to make me look crooked. I can just tell there's a coordinated effort to discredit me. 

So... I guess I can't really consider that. Because I'm certain of what's happening.

Outside of work, in your personal relationships or other areas of your life, do you generally find that people are trustworthy, or do you tend to notice similar patterns of people trying to undermine or deceive you in other situations as well?

No... it's not like that. My personal life is fine. 

People outside of work are... they're just normal. I don't really have any issues with them. I'd rather not talk about my private life anyway, but... no. It's just the stuff at the office. That's all it is.

Before this situation at work started, have you ever had similar experiences where you felt people were coordinating against you or trying to undermine you, even in different jobs or settings in the past?

No... I haven't. 

I've never had a problem like this before. It's just... just here, with this specific office. I don't really have anything else to say about past jobs. It's just this one.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear, or seen things that others couldn't see, especially around the time these work problems started?

No. I don't... I've never had anything like that. 

Just... no. I don't hear voices.

When you think about what's happening at work, do you see this as just people asking pointed questions about your reports, or do you believe there's a larger pattern or bigger reason behind why they're doing this to you specifically?

It's... it's not just random questions. There's a pattern to it. 

It started after I got this... county safety award. Ever since then, certain people have been twisting my inspection reports. They keep asking these pointed budget questions, like... like they're trying to make me look crooked. 

My supervisor keeps telling me it's just a normal review, but... I can tell it's not. It's a coordinated effort to discredit me. That's... that's what's happening. I don't really want to get into naming names, but they're definitely doing it on purpose.

Besides the situation at work with your supervisor and colleagues, have you noticed anything unusual or suspicious happening in other parts of your life — like with family members, friends, neighbors, or anyone else — even if it seems unrelated to work?

No. Nothing like that. 

It's... it's just work. My life outside the job is fine. I don't... there's nothing else going on with my family or anyone else. It's strictly the people at the office.

When you think about why these people specifically want to discredit you after you got the county safety award, what do you think their actual goal or reason is? What would they gain by making you look crooked?

I don't know. I mean... I guess they just want me out. 

It's... I don't really know exactly what they get out of it. They just... they don't want me there. That's all I know.

Have you noticed anything else unusual or strange happening that seems connected to this situation at work — like do you believe these people are using special methods to monitor you, or that they have unusual powers or abilities to carry out this plan against you?

No... nothing like that. 

They're just people from the office. They don't have... special powers or anything. They're just trying to push me out. That's it.

You mentioned they're trying to push you out and make you look crooked. If I'm understanding correctly, do you believe this is happening because they're jealous of your award, or do you think there's a different reason — like maybe they think you actually did something wrong, or something else entirely?

I... I don't really know. 

I just know they want me gone. I don't know if it's jealousy or... or what. I just know what they're doing. I haven't really figured out the exact reason why.

When you think about everything that's happening at work — the twisted reports, the budget questions, people trying to discredit you — does it all fit together into one clear picture for you, or does it feel more scattered and hard to connect?

I don't know about a... a clear picture. It's just what's happening. 

They mess with the reports, they bring up the budget... I don't really sit around trying to connect it all. It's just what they're doing. That's all I really look at.

Have you spent a lot of time trying to figure out all the details of what's happening — like thinking through exactly how they're coordinating, who's involved, what their plan is — or do you mostly just notice it happening without really analyzing it that deeply?

I don't really... analyze it. 

I just see what's in front of me. I don't spend time trying to map it all out or anything. It's just happening. I just try to do my job.

When you think about what's happening at work, have you thought through how all the pieces fit together — like, do you have a detailed understanding of how they're coordinating, who the main people are, what steps they're taking — or is it more that you just notice things happening without having worked out those details?

I... I think I just said that. I don't really sit around trying to figure out all the steps or who's talking to who. 

I just see what they do. The reports, the questions. I don't have some big map of it all. I just... notice it.

When you think about all of this at work — the people involved, what they're doing, why they're doing it — do you feel like you have a pretty clear, complete understanding of the whole situation, or does it feel like there are gaps or things that don't quite make sense to you?

I don't know. Like I keep saying... I don't really look at it like that. 

I'm not sure about gaps or... a complete picture or whatever. I just know what they're doing. I don't really think about it past that.

You mentioned your personal life is fine and people outside work are normal. But I want to ask specifically — in your romantic relationships or close personal relationships, have you ever felt suspicious that a partner or someone close to you was being dishonest with you, or that they were working against you in any way?

No. I don't have any problems like that. 

My girlfriend and I are fine. I don't... she's not doing anything. It's just the people at work. Like I said, outside of that, everything's normal. I don't have any reason to think she's lying to me.

You said you don't really think about how it all connects. But if I asked you to explain it to me — like, why do you think they started this right after you got the award, and how does that connect to them twisting your reports and asking about the budget — can you walk me through how you see those things being related to each other?

I don't know... I mean, I can't really walk you through it. 

I just know I got the award, and then... then they started acting weird. Twisting my reports, asking about the budget. I don't know exactly how it all connects. I just know it's happening. I don't really have an explanation for it.
Have you talked to anyone else about what's happening at work — like family, friends, or anyone outside the office — and what did you tell them about it?

I haven't really talked to anyone about it. 

I mean... I mentioned to my girlfriend that work has been stressful lately. But I didn't tell her all the details. I just... I don't see the point in bringing it up. It's work stuff. It stays at work.

Besides people trying to discredit you at work, do you have any other persistent beliefs or concerns about your health, your body, or anything else that you feel certain about even though other people don't see it the same way?

No. I mean... my health is fine. I don't have any concerns about my body or anything like that. 

It's just... just the work stuff. That's it.
